sections.title: Coding Agents with an Obstacle-Aware Harness for Safe Robot Manipulation
sections.abstract: The paper evaluates coding agents that write robot controllers under obstacle-avoidance constraints and introduces SafeHarness, combining obstacle-aware route planning with obstacle-aware contact execution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that SafeHarness raises task success by 6.5 percentage points and collision avoidance by 27.0 points over prior state of the art.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not establish transfer beyond the tested manipulation tasks or obstacle configurations.

sections.title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
sections.abstract: Workspace Models distill train-time VLM judgments about task-relevant history into a lightweight workspace token that replaces expensive VLM reasoning at deployment.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that workspace tokens solve memory-intensive tasks without VLM reasoning in the loop and can improve policy performance while reducing deployment cost.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not quantify the hardware-task range or memory failure modes.

sections.title: Can 4D Foundation Models Remember?
sections.abstract: PersistBench uses omniscient 360-degree video ground truth to measure object permanence, motion continuity, and appearance preservation in 4D foundation models.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that current models maintain only short-term consistency and degrade markedly after objects leave the field of view.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not specify model coverage or whether PersistBench predicts downstream navigation performance.

sections.title: Paint-Anything: Unified Any-Color Control for Image Generation and Editing
sections.abstract: Paint-Anything trains a shared hex-prompt interface for object-level 24-bit color control in text-to-image generation and editing, with Paint-500K and the ACBench benchmark.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 85.3% and 28.3% relative gains on ACBench-T2I and ACBench-Edit.
sections.caveat: The headline improvements are reported on the authors' benchmark and a FLUX.2-4B base.

sections.title: An Analysis of Training-Free Self-Reported Confidence in Language Models
sections.abstract: On 100 TriviaQA questions and two model families, the study compares verbalized confidence, post-hoc P(True), and three-sample agreement as training-free correctness signals.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report AUROC 0.956 and 0.937 for verbalized confidence in this setup, while self-consistency can amplify shared misconceptions.
sections.caveat: The sample is small and should not be treated as a general calibration guarantee.

sections.title: Language-model groups overstate consensus when replaying human deliberation on a reasoning task
sections.abstract: Replaying 100 held-out human Wason groups with matched LLM groups, the study finds that model groups appear substantially more consensual and that consensus does not track collective accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper reports 34.0–44.4 percentage-point consensus gaps under participation and submission controls.
sections.caveat: The evidence comes from one reasoning task and replay design.

sections.title: UnifiedPlayers: Enhance Tool-Integrated Reasoning in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
sections.abstract: UnifiedPlayers jointly trains planning, execution, and evaluation players so tool-using agents can generate trajectories and adaptive executable verifiers under GRPO.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report gains of at least 3.5% on mathematical reasoning and 3.9% on general reasoning over the strongest prior baseline.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not identify all baselines or establish behavior under broader distribution shift.

sections.title: OmniMimic: Dynamics-completed Motion Augmentation for Multi-style Omnidirectional Quadruped Locomotion
sections.abstract: OmniMimic expands directionally limited animal demonstrations into multi-gait quadruped policies using dynamics completion, temporal reversal, reflection, progressive command expansion, and gait-specialized residual experts.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 12.9% lower mean foot-position RMSE and 63.1% lower velocity-tracking RMSE against a matched baseline.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not establish real-robot transfer or robustness to demonstration mismatch.
